title: Why the Developer Wants Your Off-Plan Deal to Win, and What to Check

keywords: can I trust an off-plan developer
body:
Many people think buying off-plan means trusting the developer blindly. You hand over a deposit for a building that does not exist and hope for the best. I see it differently. Do not start with trust. Start with the math.

## The math behind the deal

If you make one dollar on your unit, the developer makes about ten on the entire project. You have one unit at stake. The developer has the whole building at stake.

That simple ratio changes how you should look at the deal. You are not the person with the most to gain or the most to lose. The developer is.

## Everything depends on finishing this building

For the developer, this project is not one investment among many. Three things ride on it:

- **Their profit.** The money is only made when the project is finished and delivered.
- **Their reputation.** Every finished building is proof for the next group of buyers. Every failure follows them.
- **Their next building.** Without a delivered project, the next one is much harder to sell.

So the developer will fight harder than you to deliver. Not because they are nice. Because they have the most to lose.

## Aligned interests are not a guarantee

This does not mean every project is safe. A developer can want to deliver and still not be able to. Interests can be aligned and the execution can still fail. That is why the next step matters.

## Your job is to check, not to trust

Your job is not to trust the developer. Your job is to check that they can do it. The best place to start is their track record:

1. Look at the buildings they have already finished.
2. See whether those buildings match what was promised to buyers.
3. Find out whether they delivered on time.

A developer with a history of finished projects has shown they can do what they are promising you now. A developer with no history is asking you to take more on faith.

## The bottom line

The developer wants your deal to win, because your deal is part of their deal. Use that to feel calmer about off-plan, but do not use it as a reason to skip your homework. Check the record, then decide.

faq: Can you trust an off-plan developer?
You do not need blind trust. The developer usually has far more at stake than any single buyer, but you should still verify that they can deliver by checking their past projects.
How do I check an off-plan developer's track record?
Look at the buildings they have already completed, compare them with what was promised to buyers, and check whether they were delivered on time.
Why does a developer want to finish an off-plan project?
Their profit, their reputation and their ability to sell the next project all depend on delivering the current one.
